citations.B1: Read-then-write on `counts` is not atomic, so two threads can both pass the check and exceed the limit
citations.B3: hold a lock (or use a single atomic operation) around the read/increment
citations.B4: There is no time window at all, so counts only ever grow and every user is permanently banned after 100 requests
citations.B5: Nothing ever removes entries, so the dictionary grows without bound and leaks memory
citations.B6: `counts` is per-process, so N workers each allow the full limit and the real ceiling is N × limit
citations.B7: Unhashable or `None` user IDs raise or collapse into one shared bucket — validate the key before use.
